messages:
sara: Quick postmortem follow-up for last night's KV OOM. Short summary: recurring heap fragmentation + long-lived small allocations in the shard cache. I sketched a 3-tier plan (short mitigations, telemetry, allocator changes). Please read and claim items.

sara: Action table (short):
1) emergency shard eviction cap (soft limit) -> owner: ? -> ETA: 24h
2) targeted heap profile across 3 failing hosts -> owner: ? -> ETA: 48h
3) enable aggressive slab compaction on canary region -> owner: ? -> ETA: 72h
4) checksum/validate cache pointers after recent change -> owner: ? -> ETA: end of sprint

liam: I'll take (1) emergency soft cap. can do a config flip and a quick smoke. ETA 6h. What should the cap be?

sara: @liam thanks. start with cap = 85% of current shard memory allotment, then tune. Put rollout as canary -> region-us-west-2 -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

emily: I'll pick (2) profiles. plan: run `heap-sample --pid $PID --duration 120s --out s3://redwood-debug/kv-profiles/` on three hosts (a,b,c). I'll also upload flamegraphs. ETA 36h.

raj: Re: (3) slab compaction — I want to try the new compaction heuristic (compact_threshold=0.2) on the canary. If it reduces fragmentation, we can bake into runtime. I'll own the canary rollout and monitor tail latency. ETA 48h.

sara: (4) pointer validation is higher-risk. @raj / @emily can you pair for a short audit of the pointer-affecting change in shard sync? I'd rather have a quick code review before we roll.

emily: sure. can do a 1h audit tomorrow morning. tagging `ops-bot` to capture traces and span correlation.

ops-bot: [automated] Created ticket INF-6423: "KV heap fragmentation follow-up" assigned to unassigned. Link: https://issue.redwood/INF-6423

liam: quick question on telemetry: what event should we add to catch pre-oom fragmentation spikes? we currently report total-allocated but not free-run fragmentation ratio.

raj: propose metric `kv.frag_ratio = free_bytes / total_allocated_bytes` sampled every 10s per shard. alert if > 0.3 for 5m. Also emit `kv.evictions.timed` when soft cap triggers.

sara: good metric. add it to dashboards and set a low-severity alert for now. @emily can you add the metric to the profile ingestion pipeline?

emily: yes, will add a lightweight sampler to the agent and a quick parser for flamegraph tags. also adding a replication of the profile to dev environment for faster iteration.

liam: regarding mitigation rollout steps (for clarity):
- change config in runtime repo `configs/eviction.toml`
- create canary PR -> CI -> deploy to us-west-2
- monitor `kv.evictions.timed`, `srv.errors.oom`, `p99.latency`
- rollback on p99 > baseline + 15% or srv.errors.oom > 0

sara: perfect. can someone own the rollback playbook doc? we should add exact commands: `redwood deploy rollback --target kv-runtime --to previous` and quick sysctl knobs.

raj: I'll write the rollback doc. will include commands + Grafana links. ETA 12h.

liam: done with initial cap PR, created branch `liam/eviction-cap`. link: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/812 — small config change only. canary deploy in 30m.

emily: started heap-sample on host-a. sample id: hs-210334. uploading now.

sara: checklist for 48h: confirm (1) cap in canary, (2) 3 profiles collected, (3) compaction heuristic trial started, (4) metrics added. After that we'll decide whether to schedule allocator refactor in next sprint.

liam: can we add a retrospective tag to the ticket so recurring incidents show up? set `incident_tag=kv-frag-2026`.

ops-bot: [automated] Ticket INF-6423 updated: tags added {"kv-frag-2026"}

raj: one more thing: add a GC-friendly path for long-lived allocations: move small objects to a separate slab class to reduce cross-slab fragmentation. that requires a touch in the allocator; estimate ~2w engineering. Will propose RFC if short-term mitigations look good.

sara: thanks all. next check-in in ~36h to confirm progress. If anyone hits blockers ping here and @sara directly. :thumbsup:
